root_cause.text: In `drivers/irqchip/irq-mchp-eic.c`, `mchp_eic_domain_alloc()` validated the translated `hwirq` against `MCHP_EIC_NIRQ` but, when `irq_domain_translate_twocell()` produced an out-of-range value, it returned success (`ret` was 0) instead of `-EINVAL`, allowing later out-of-bounds access in the Microchip EIC IRQ domain code.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `if (ret || hwirq >= MCHP_EIC_NIRQ) return ret;` to `return ret ?: -EINVAL;`, and the CVE description states that when `irq_domain_translate_twocell()` sets `hwirq >= MCHP_EIC_NIRQ (2)` it “results in an out of bounds access” because “the code checks for invalid values, but doesn't set the error code.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Reject invalid IRQ domain translations by returning -EINVAL when the translated hardware IRQ is out of range.
intent_record.what: In mchp_eic_domain_alloc(), the error return after irq_domain_translate_twocell() was changed from `return ret;` to `return ret ?: -EINVAL;` when either translation fails or `hwirq` is out of range.
intent_record.how: If irq_domain_translate_twocell() succeeds but produces an invalid hardware IRQ number, the function now returns -EINVAL instead of incorrectly returning 0. This ensures invalid IRQ specifiers are rejected rather than treated as successful allocation.

grouping_result.intent: Reject invalid IRQ domain translations by returning -EINVAL when the translated hardware IRQ is out of range.

relevance_review.reason: The group’s core intent exactly matches the root cause: it fixes the IRQ domain allocation path to reject out-of-range translated hwirq values with -EINVAL instead of succeeding, which prevents the out-of-bounds access.

candidates.rationale: This check was the vulnerable gate: when translation succeeded but produced an out-of-range hwirq, the code returned the existing ret value (0) instead of -EINVAL, allowing invalid IRQs to proceed.
This return statement propagates 0 on an out-of-range translated hwirq, which is the direct bug described in the root cause.

vuln_statements.explanation: When irq_domain_translate_twocell() succeeded but produced an out-of-range hwirq, this statement returned 0 instead of -EINVAL, allowing invalid IRQs to be accepted and later used out of bounds.

bic_trace_step.reason: The relevant allocation path is present in `mchp_eic_domain_alloc()`, and it already rejects out-of-range hardware IRQs correctly: `ret = irq_domain_translate_twocell(domain, fwspec, &hwirq, &type); if (ret || hwirq >= MCHP_EIC_NIRQ) return ret;`. This means an out-of-range `hwirq` is not converted into success; it returns the translation result (or an error if translation failed), so the vulnerable construct described in the root cause is not present in this snippet.
